request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient, an 83-year-old woman with a history of developmental disorders, presented to the emergency outpatient unit with a one-week history of dyspnea. She had heavily decreased breath sounds in the left lung. Chest radiograph and CT scan of the chest showed pleural effusions on the left lung. Two diagnostic thoracenteses were non-diagnostic, and a semirigid thoracoscopy was performed to visualize the pleura. Thoracoscopy revealed diffuse thickening of the parietal and visceral pleura, compatible with pleural dissemination with biopsy samples taken from only the visceral pleura node. Hematoxylin and eosin staining and immunohistochemical staining revealed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma with malignant neoplasm. 
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Disposition:
The patient was discharged to the care of her family. 

Condition:
The patient had a stable condition upon discharge. 

Clinical Course:
The patient required semirigid thoracoscopy with biopsy samples taken from only the visceral pleura node. Hematoxylin and eosin staining and immunohistochemical staining revealed a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma.

Follow-up:
The patient was referred for follow-up care with an oncologist. 

Instructions:
The patient was instructed to follow-up with an oncologist. 

Treatment:
The patient underwent semirigid thoracoscopy for biopsy samples, which was successful. The treatment plan includes referral to an oncologist for further management. 

Complications:
No complications were noted during the hospitalization.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode was an investigation that ended in a diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma, with pleural dissemination and malignant effusion. In ICD-10-AM, the principal diagnosis is the condition established after study to be chiefly responsible for the admission. That condition is the primary lung cancer, which is coded to C34 (malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung).

The alternative is C78.2 (secondary malignant neoplasm of pleura), but the primary site is known to be lung, so the lung cancer takes precedence. The pleural effusion is a manifestation of the malignancy, and the pleural metastasis would be a secondary code.

CODE: C34
